mainTopic: The offspring and תמורה of שלמים: their status, their sources in the פסוקים, and their limits.
overview: This amud begins by finishing a defense of שמואל: the תנא brought against him may rely on the rule that an animal unfit for the מזבח cannot get קדושת הגוף, so he is no proof against שמואל. Then פרק יש בקרבנות ends, and פרק אלו קדשים begins. Its משנה teaches that the offspring and the תמורה of שלמים, for all generations, are full שלמים. The גמרא explains that 'until the end of the world' is aimed against רבי אלעזר. A ברייתא learns the rule from 'זכר' and 'נקבה' in the פסוק, and from 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה' for animals that come from blemished ones. אביי defends this matching against רב ספרא's challenges. שמואל and בר פדא then argue whether the offspring of a blemished שלמים is actually offered or only left to graze. Another ברייתא learns the rule from 'רק קדשיך… תשא ובאת', and the גמרא examines its lines. The amud ends by asking which offspring the word 'רק' could possibly exclude. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל could say this תנא follows a different principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends שמואל by suggesting that the תנא quoted against him might also hold that קדושת הגוף cannot rest on an animal that is not fit to be offered itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could answer you: maybe this תנא also holds that whenever an animal is not fit to be offered itself, קדושת הגוף does not come onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a discussion from before this section. It answers a challenge against שמואל by showing that the source used against him may not really disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge treated this תנא's ruling as a proof against שמואל. The answer is that this תנא may base his ruling on a different principle: an animal unfit for the altar cannot get קדושת הגוף. שמואל himself follows the opinion that disagrees with that principle, so the source is no proof against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that rests on the animal's body itself, so the animal itself becomes a קרבן (as opposed to holiness of value, where only its money value is holy)
Fit to be offered itself
Maybe, perhaps; often used to offer a possible way out of a challenge
Comes down onto, takes effect on

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
Perhaps this tanna also holds
that anywhere that it is not fit itself,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the animal. It cannot be offered on the מזבח as it is.

phrases.english: inherent sanctity does not come upon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: דִּלְמָא הָךְ תַּנָּא נָמֵי סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge against שמואל raised before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the opposing source as agreeing with שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought this תנא's ruling proves something against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא may also hold that an animal unfit for the altar does not get קדושת הגוף, so there is no proof against שמואל.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter יש בקרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter יש בקרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יש בקרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the פרק called יש בקרבנות. This is a closing line, not an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional formula said when finishing a פרק. It shows love for the learning and a hope to come back to it. Nothing legal is being said here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a chapter
Chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Yesh BeKorbanot.
phrases.notes: 'יש בקרבנות' is the name of the chapter, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק יש בקרבנות is complete.

steps.title: Offspring and substitutes of peace offerings are peace offerings forever
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the offspring and תמורה of שלמים, and their offspring for all generations, are שלמים with all the requirements of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the קדשים whose offspring and substitutes are like them: the offspring of שלמים and their substitutes, and the offspring of those, and the offspring of their offspring, until the end of the world. They are all שלמים, and they need סמיכה, נסכים, and the waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. The משנה teaches that when an animal of שלמים gives birth or is substituted, the new animal is also a full קרבן שלמים, generation after generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness of שלמים passes to the offspring and to the תמורה, and from them onward forever. These animals are treated exactly like regular שלמים: someone does סמיכה on them, they are brought with נסכים, and the חזה ושוק are waved and given to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Offspring, a newborn animal
A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן, which then also becomes holy
Peace offerings
Leaning one's hands on the head of the קרבן
Waving the breast and the thigh, which are then given to the כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the topic for the whole new פרק: how holiness carries over to offspring and substitutes. It also sets up the argument with רבי אלעזר that the גמרא is about to bring.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are the sacrificial animals
whose offspring and substitutes are like them:
the offspring of peace offerings and their substitutes,
their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring,
until the end of all the world:
they are peace offerings,
and they require placing hands and libations,
and the waving of the breast and the thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ קָדָשִׁים שֶׁוַּולְדוֹתֵיהֶן וּתְמוּרוֹתֵיהֶן כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring and substitutes of שלמים, for all generations, are full שלמים and need סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופת חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Why add 'until the end of the world'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the words 'until the end of the world' after it already said 'their offspring and the offspring of their offspring'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה already taught 'their offspring and the offspring of their offspring', why do I need 'until the end of all the world'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's wording. The extra phrase seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה says the holiness passes to the next generation and to the one after that, we already understand it keeps going. So 'until the end of the world' looks extra. The גמרא assumes no words in a משנה are wasted and asks what they add.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה; marks the start of the גמרא
Since he already taught
Why do I need it? A question about wording that seems extra

phrases.english: GEMARA: Since he taught
'their offspring and the offspring of their offspring,'
why do I need 'until the end of all the world'?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּתְנָא ״וְלָדָן וּוְלַד וְלָדָן״, ״עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'עד סוף כל העולם' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Their offspring and the offspring of their offspring' already shows the holiness continues, so the extra phrase seems unneeded.

steps.title: The extra words answer רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The תנא added 'until the end of the world' to argue strongly against רבי אלעזר, who holds that the offspring of שלמים may not be offered as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא heard that רבי אלעזר said the offspring of שלמים may not be offered as שלמים. Our תנא said to him: I don't agree with you about the direct offspring, and I don't agree with you even about all the generations until the end of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The extra words are there to reject רבי אלעזר's view as strongly as possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר, whose view appears in the next משנה, holds that even the first offspring of שלמים is not offered. Our תנא disagrees completely. He says even the farthest generations are offered as שלמים, so 'until the end of the world' is an emphatic disagreement, not extra wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of our משנה
Not only ... but even; a 'this is obvious, and even more' pattern
I agree, I concede
Shall not be offered

steps.whatToRemember: Our תנא says the offspring of שלמים are offered as שלמים forever. רבי אלעזר says even the first offspring is not offered. 'Until the end of the world' expresses our תנא's full disagreement with him.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לא מיבעיא ... אלא אפילו' does not mean our תנא agrees about the first offspring. He disagrees about the first offspring and, all the more so, about every later generation.

phrases.english: Our tanna heard Rabbi Elazar
who said, 'The offspring of a peace offering is not offered as a peace offering,'
phrases.notes: This view of רבי אלעזר appears in the next משנה.

phrases.english: and our tanna said to him:
It is not necessary to say that about their offspring I do not concede,
but even until the end of the world
I do not concede to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 about the extra words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the extra wording is an emphatic disagreement with another opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until the end of the world' seemed to repeat what 'offspring of offspring' already said.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase rejects רבי אלעזר completely: every generation of offspring is offered as שלמים.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the offspring and תמורה of שלמים are offered as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated that the offspring and תמורה of שלמים are themselves שלמים. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה's wording to looking for its source in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that the offspring and תמורה of שלמים are offered.

steps.title: The word 'male' includes the offspring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'זכר' that the offspring of שלמים is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Male' comes to include the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: the word 'זכר' in the פסוק about שלמים adds the offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about שלמים says 'אם זכר אם נקבה', and the word 'זכר' looks extra. The ברייתא uses that extra word to include the offspring of a שלמים animal.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add something through an extra word)
Offspring of a consecrated animal
Male (a word in the פסוק about שלמים)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'Male' — to include the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'זכר' in the פסוק about שלמים includes the offspring.

steps.title: Why not learn it from a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed. If a תמורה, which did not grow from הקדש, is offered, the offspring, which did grow from הקדש, should surely be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it logical? If a תמורה, which did not grow out of הקדש, is offered, then the offspring, which did grow out of הקדש, should surely be offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own source. It argues that we could know the offspring is offered through simple logic, without a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה is just an ordinary animal that got holiness by being swapped, yet it is offered. The offspring actually grew out of a holy animal, so it seems even stronger. This קל וחומר would make the word 'זכר' unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? (opens a קל וחומר that makes a פסוק seem unneeded)
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Something that grew out of a consecrated item
An animal swapped for a consecrated animal, which also becomes holy

phrases.english: But is it not a logical inference?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה תְּמוּרָה, שֶׁאֵין גִּידּוּלֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ — קְרֵיבָה,
phrases.english: If a substitute, which did not grow from consecrated property, is offered,
then the offspring, which did grow from consecrated property,
is it not logical that it should be offered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the source in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the word 'זכר' to include the offspring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from תמורה already proves the offspring is offered, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The קל וחומר is knocked down
steps.stepSummary: תמורה applies to all קדשים, but offspring does not, so the offspring might be weaker and not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about תמורה? It applies to all sacrifices. Can you say the same about offspring, which does not apply to all sacrifices? Maybe it is not offered, since it does not apply to all sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא breaks the קל וחומר by showing that תמורה has a strength that offspring lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any consecrated animal can have a תמורה. Not every sacrifice can have offspring, for example a male animal. Since the two cases are each stronger in a different way, we cannot learn one from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X, which has this special feature? (a way of breaking a קל וחומר)
Applies to all consecrated animals
Since, because

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִתְמוּרָה, שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: What about a substitute? It applies to all consecrated animals.

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּוָלָד, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים?
phrases.english: Will you say the same about offspring, which does not apply to all consecrated animals?

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ קָרֵב הוֹאִיל וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: It should not be offered, since it does not apply to all consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִתְמוּרָה, שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר raised in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר from תמורה to offspring.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תמורה is stronger in one way: it applies to all קדשים. So the offspring cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: 'Male' teaches offspring, 'female' teaches תמורה
steps.stepSummary: Since logic fails, the פסוק is needed: 'זכר' includes the offspring and 'נקבה' includes the תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says 'male' to include the offspring, and 'female' to include the תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the קל וחומר failed, the ברייתא goes back to the פסוק. It uses each word for one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זכר' is truly needed for the offspring. The word 'נקבה' is used to teach that a תמורה of שלמים is offered as שלמים. Each case now has its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (introduces the source)
Female (another word in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring of שלמים comes from 'זכר'. תמורה of שלמים comes from 'נקבה'.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states 'male,' to include the offspring,
and 'female,' to include the substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical argument fails, it confirms that the פסוק is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the offspring and the תמורה of שלמים are offered as שלמים, learned from 'זכר' and 'נקבה'.

steps.title: What about animals that come from blemished ones?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that the offspring and תמורה of blemished animals are also offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about the תמורה and offspring of unblemished animals. How do I know about the offspring and תמורה of blemished animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the rule also covers animals that come from blemished consecrated animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'זכר' and 'נקבה' only cover cases that come from a perfect animal. A blemished animal cannot be offered itself. So the ברייתא needs a new source to show that its offspring or תמורה can be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (that much so far)
Unblemished animals
Blemished animals
From where do we know?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא תְּמוּרַת תְּמִימִין, וּוְלַד תְּמִימִין,
phrases.english: I have only the substitute of unblemished animals and the offspring of unblemished animals;

phrases.aramaic: וְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין וּתְמוּרַת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: from where do I know the offspring of blemished animals and the substitute of blemished animals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule from step 10 to a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the offspring and תמורה of blemished consecrated animals are offered.

steps.title: 'If male' and 'if female' include the blemished cases
steps.stepSummary: The longer wording 'אם זכר' includes the offspring of blemished animals, and 'אם נקבה' includes the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'if male' to include the offspring of blemished animals, and 'if female' to include the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the extra word 'אם' ('if') before each word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words already taught the cases of unblemished animals. The extra 'אם' adds the cases of blemished animals. Offspring is still learned from 'זכר' and תמורה from 'נקבה', so each case keeps its own word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If male… if female': the fuller wording of the פסוק, used to add more cases

steps.whatToRemember: Plain 'זכר' and 'נקבה' cover animals that come from unblemished ones. 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה' add animals that come from blemished ones.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם זָכָר״ לְרַבּוֹת וְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין,
phrases.english: The verse states 'if male,' to include the offspring of blemished animals,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1. The extra word 'אם' is what adds the new case.

phrases.english: and 'if female,' to include the substitute of blemished animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם זָכָר״ לְרַבּוֹת וְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'אם' before 'זכר' and 'נקבה' includes the offspring and תמורה of blemished animals.

steps.title: רב ספרא asks why we cannot reverse the derivation
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges אביי: why not reverse the teaching, and say 'אם זכר' includes the תמורה of blemished animals and 'אם נקבה' includes their offspring?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to אביי: I could reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks the matching we just learned in step 12. He says the words could be assigned the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, 'אם זכר' was used for the offspring of blemished animals and 'אם נקבה' for their תמורה. רב ספרא asks what forces that order. Nothing in the extra words themselves seems to choose one way over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I could reverse it.' A challenge saying the opposite reading works just as well

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Abaye:
But I could reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means swapping what 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה' teach in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the matching of words to cases given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of 'אם זכר' to the offspring and 'אם נקבה' to the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words could just as easily be matched the opposite way.

steps.title: אביי: the same word should teach about the same kind of animal
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that it makes sense for the word that included the תמורה of unblemished animals to also include the תמורה of blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense: from the same place that the substitute of unblemished animals was included, the substitute of blemished animals is included.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the order from step 12. He says the matching follows the matching already set up in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, 'נקבה' included the תמורה of unblemished animals. So the longer form 'אם נקבה' should include the תמורה of blemished animals too. Each word stays with the same kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is logical
Unblemished animals
Blemished animals

phrases.english: It makes sense,
that from the place where the substitute of unblemished animals was included,
the substitute of blemished animals is included.
phrases.notes: The 'place' is the word נקבה. Plain 'נקבה' taught step 10, and 'אם נקבה' teaches this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical consistency: each word keeps teaching about the same kind of animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה' could be swapped freely.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אם נקבה' goes with the תמורה, just as 'נקבה' did in step 10.

steps.title: רב ספרא clarifies: reverse the whole verse
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that he meant reversing the whole פסוק: 'זכר' would include the תמורה and 'נקבה' would include the offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did I tell you to reverse only 'אם זכר' and 'אם נקבה'? I am talking about the whole verse! Say: 'זכר' includes the substitute, and 'נקבה' includes the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא says אביי misunderstood him. He wants to swap the teaching of step 10 too, not only the teaching of step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer only works if step 10 stays in place. רב ספרא says: swap step 10 as well. Then 'זכר' and 'אם זכר' would cover the תמורה, and 'נקבה' and 'אם נקבה' would cover the offspring. That way each word still stays with one kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole verse
To include

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did I tell you to reverse
only 'if male' and 'if female'?
I am talking about the whole verse!
Say: 'male' comes to include the substitute,
and 'female' comes to include the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the challenge so that אביי's answer in step 14 no longer works.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole matching of 'זכר' to the offspring and 'נקבה' to the תמורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both steps 10 and 12 are swapped together, the 'same word, same kind of animal' logic still holds, so that logic cannot decide the order.

steps.title: אביי: the words themselves are masculine and feminine
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'ולד' is a masculine word, so it fits 'זכר', and 'תמורה' is a feminine word, so it fits 'נקבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'ולד' sounds masculine, and 'תמורה' sounds feminine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer based on grammar. This answer works even against the bigger challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Hebrew, the word 'ולד' (offspring) is masculine, and 'תמורה' (substitute) is feminine. So it is natural for 'זכר' (male) to include the ולד and for 'נקבה' (female) to include the תמורה. This settles the order of the whole פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A masculine word form
A feminine word form
It means; it sounds like

steps.confusionAlert: This is about the grammar of the words 'ולד' and 'תמורה', not about whether the actual animals are male or female.
steps.whatToRemember: 'זכר' and 'אם זכר' include the offspring; 'נקבה' and 'אם נקבה' include the תמורה. The reason is grammar: 'ולד' is masculine and 'תמורה' is feminine.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'Offspring' is a masculine word,
and 'substitute' is a feminine word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the stronger challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grammatical fit between the word in the פסוק and the word for the animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק could be read in reverse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The masculine word 'ולד' goes with 'זכר', and the feminine word 'תמורה' goes with 'נקבה'.

steps.title: What practical law is being taught?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law comes from the rule that the offspring of a blemished animal has קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new question about the ברייתא of step 12. It asks what the ruling about the offspring of a blemished animal means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the offspring of a blemished שלמים 'is like a שלמים' could mean two things. Maybe it can actually be offered on the מזבח. Or maybe it only has some lesser kind of holiness. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical result?

phrases.english: For what law?
phrases.notes: This asks about the ruling in step 12, that the offspring of a blemished animal is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the grammar debate and returns to the ruling of step 12 to clarify its practical meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical status the offspring of a blemished קרבן has.

steps.title: שמואל: it is actually offered, following רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the offspring may actually be offered on the מזבח, and the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: to be offered, and this follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question of step 17. The offspring of a blemished animal is brought as a real קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the mother cannot go on the מזבח because of her blemish, her offspring can. שמואל ties this to רבי אלעזר, who holds that an offspring can be offered even when its mother cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered on the מזבח
According to the opinion of

phrases.english: Shmuel said: For it to be offered,
and this follows the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר holds that the male offspring of a female set aside as an עולה is itself offered as an עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offspring of a blemished שלמים is actually offered, following רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא still needed to teach this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have limited רבי אלעזר's rule to an עולה, since a female עולה exists for birds. So the ברייתא teaches that even these offspring of blemished animals are offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because you might have said: when רבי אלעזר spoke, it was about an עולה, since the name עולה can apply to its mother. But these offspring are not offered. So the ברייתא teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא is not repeating what רבי אלעזר already said. It shows that the new case could have been different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's case, the mother is a female, and a female can be an עולה in some cases, such as birds. So the mother is not totally unfit for that status. A blemished animal, however, can never be a שלמים, so we might think its offspring cannot be offered. The ברייתא teaches that it is offered anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken thought)
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)
The name or status of an עולה

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the offspring of a blemished שלמים is actually offered. This goes even further than רבי אלעזר's case of an עולה.

phrases.english: Because you might have said:
when Rabbi Elazar spoke, it was about a burnt offering,
since the name of a burnt offering can apply to its mother,
phrases.notes: A female can be an עולה in the case of birds, so the mother is not totally outside that status.

phrases.english: but these offspring are not offered,
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא was needed, given שמואל's link to רבי אלעזר in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the new case is a bigger step than the known case (מהו דתימא, קמשמע לן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's rule might apply only to an עולה, where the mother can have that status in some cases, and not to the offspring of a blemished animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the offspring of a blemished שלמים is offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: A second answer: the offspring is left to graze
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא says the practical law is that the offspring must graze until it gets a blemish, and this fits everyone's view. רבא and רב פפא have the same argument as שמואל and בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא says: the law is that it is left to graze, and this works according to everyone. As it was taught: רבא says it is offered, following רבי אלעזר. רב פפא says it is left to graze, following everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from step 17: what practical law comes from saying the offspring of a blemished animal has קדושה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the offspring is actually offered on the מזבח, but that only fits רבי אלעזר. בר פדא says its קדושה only means it cannot be used freely. It must graze until it becomes blemished, and this works even for those who argue with רבי אלעזר. The same argument appears between רבא (offered) and רב פפא (grazing).

keyTerms.meaning: For grazing: the animal is left to pasture until it gets a blemish, and it is not offered
To be offered on the מזבח
Everyone's opinion, meaning even the חכמים who argue would agree

steps.confusionAlert: רעיה here does not mean the animal is offered later. It means the animal is holy enough that you cannot use it. You leave it to graze until it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: Bar Padda says: for grazing,
and this is according to everyone's opinion.
As it was stated: Rava says: to be offered,
and this is according to Rabbi Elazar.
Rav Pappa says: for grazing,
and this is according to everyone's opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר פְּדָא אָמַר: לִרְעִיָּה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from שמואל's answer to the question in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law results from the offspring of a blemished animal having קדושה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It must graze until it gets a blemish (רעיה), and this works for everyone. רבא and רב פפא disagree in the same way.

steps.title: Another תנא learns the law from a פסוק in דברים
steps.stepSummary: A different תנא learns the law of תמורה and offspring from 'רק קדשיך אשר יהיו לך תשא ובאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא brings the law from here: 'Only your holy things' refers to substitutes. 'That you have' refers to offspring. 'You shall take and go' to the chosen place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different תנא who learns the law of תמורה and offspring from a new פסוק. This sets up the next back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא learned the law of the תמורה and offspring of שלמים from the extra words 'זכר' and 'נקבה'. This תנא reads דברים 12:26 instead. 'קדשיך' means the תמורה, 'אשר יהיו לך' means the offspring, and 'תשא ובאת' means both must be brought to the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן. It becomes holy too
Offspring born to a קרבן animal
'You shall take and go': bring it to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And this tanna brings it from here.
'Only your holy things': these are the substitutes,
'that you have': these are the offspring,
'you shall take and go.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different תנא's source for the law of תמורה and offspring
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמורה and offspring of קדשים must be brought to the בית המקדש

steps.title: Maybe bringing them in is enough, even if they just die there
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the פסוק might only require bringing the animals to the בית המקדש and then leaving them without food and water until they die.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a person should bring them into the בית המקדש and keep water and food from them so that they die.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wrong reading of 'תשא ובאת'. This sets up the next proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תשא ובאת' only says to bring the animals. It does not say what to do with them after that. So we might think they are just brought in and left to die, and not actually offered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a wrong idea that the ברייתא will then reject
The chosen house, meaning the בית המקדש

phrases.english: One might think he should bring it into the Temple,
and withhold water and food from them
so that they die?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible narrow reading of the פסוק from step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'תשא ובאת' require only bringing the animals, so they could be left to die?

steps.title: They are treated like a real עולה or שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The next words of the פסוק, 'ועשית עולותיך הבשר והדם', teach that the תמורה and offspring are actually offered, just like the original קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood.' Just as you treat an עולה, you treat its substitute. Just as you treat שלמים, you treat the offspring of שלמים and its substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the wrong idea with the next words of the פסוק: the animals are actually offered on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks right away about offering 'the flesh and the blood' of the קרבנות. This shows the animals brought in are offered, not left to die. Each one follows the rules of its original קרבן: an עולה's תמורה is offered as an עולה, and the offspring and תמורה of שלמים are offered as שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': brings the proof that rejects the wrong idea
A burnt offering that is fully burned on the מזבח
A peace offering that is partly eaten by the owners

steps.whatToRemember: The תמורה and the offspring of קדשים are brought to the בית המקדש and offered there. Each one follows the rules of the original קרבן.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood,'
in the way that you treat a burnt offering,
you treat the substitute,
in the way that you treat a peace offering,
you treat the offspring of a peace offering and the substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְעָשִׂיתָ עוֹלוֹתֶיךָ הַבָּשָׂר וְהַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wrong idea from step 22 using the next words of the פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תמורה and offspring are offered just like the original עולה or שלמים, not left to die

steps.title: Does this apply to every kind of קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether every קרבן's תמורה and offspring are offered like the original animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think all sacrificial animals are like this.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It has just taught that the תמורה and offspring are offered like the original קרבן, and now it asks whether that is true for every type of קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 showed that the תמורה and offspring are really brought on the מזבח. Now the ברייתא tests how far that rule reaches. Maybe it covers every kind of קדשים with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': it opens a possible idea that the ברייתא will then correct
Holy animals set aside as קרבנות

phrases.english: One might think that all sacrificial animals are like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the rule from step 23 reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule that the תמורה and offspring are offered applies to all קדשים

steps.title: The word 'רק' limits the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says the word 'רק' teaches that the rule does not apply to every קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'Only'. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 24. The word 'רק' at the start of the פסוק shows that the rule is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דרשה, the word 'רק' usually signals that something is left out. So the ברייתא reads it as removing some קרבנות from the rule, meaning their תמורה and offspring are not offered. The ברייתא names this as the view of רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': it brings in a word or phrase as the source
'Only': a word that limits and leaves something out

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Only'
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not every קרבן is included, because 'רק' leaves some out

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: 'אשם הוא' already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the word 'רק' is not needed for this, because 'אשם הוא' already shows that an אשם's תמורה is not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: it is not needed. The פסוק already says 'It is an אשם; he is certainly guilty before ה׳'. It is offered, but its תמורה is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different source. He says we do not need 'רק', because a different פסוק already teaches that an אשם's תמורה is not brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא focuses on the word 'הוא' ('it'). The פסוק says 'it', the אשם itself, is offered, which leaves out its תמורה. Both תנאים agree on the law, and they only disagree about where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed': there is no need for that source
A guilt offering
An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן. It becomes holy too.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not disagree about the law. He only says the source is a different פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: It is not necessary,
for the verse already says
'It is a guilt offering; he is certainly guilty before the Lord'
'It' is sacrificed,
but its substitute is not sacrificed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the limit taught in step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמורה of an אשם is not offered, learned from 'אשם הוא'
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree that some תמורות are not offered. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'רק', and רבי עקיבא learns it from 'אשם הוא'.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא again: 'bring it to the בית הבחירה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and quotes the line of the ברייתא that suggested the animals might just be brought to the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'You shall take and go'. One might think he should bring it into the בית הבחירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes again the line from step 22 so that it can question it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the ברייתא suggested that 'תשא ובאת' might only mean bringing the animals in and leaving them to die. The גמרא repeats that line now because it wants to ask where such an idea could even come from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The chosen house': the בית המקדש
'You shall take and go': the words in the פסוק about bringing the animals

phrases.english: The Master said: 'You shall take and go,'
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא in steps 22 and 23. The פסוק is דברים 12:26.

phrases.english: one might think he should bring it into the Temple?
phrases.notes: He means bringing it in and leaving it there without food or water until it dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא line from step 22 to examine it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeats the ברייתא's suggestion that the animals are brought in and left to die

steps.title: Why would anyone think they are left to die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this idea comes from. Only the חמש חטאות are known to be left to die, so these other animals should obviously be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where would you get this idea? Since we have a tradition about the five חטאות that die, these others should be offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's suggestion. It asks why anyone would think the animals are left to die, since we already know exactly which animals are left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a הלכה למשה מסיני that five kinds of חטאת are left to die. Because that list is set, it seems that any other holy animal, like the offspring or תמורה of a שלמים, should simply be offered. So the ברייתא's suggestion looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Where would you get this from?': it challenges where an idea comes from
The five kinds of חטאת that are left to die, known by tradition
'They learned it': known by tradition
'They are surely offered'

phrases.english: From where would this come?
Since they learned by tradition about five sin offerings,
phrases.notes: These are the five kinds of חטאת that are left to die, known as a הלכה למשה מסיני.

phrases.english: these others are certainly offered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion quoted in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that the animals might be brought in and left to die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tradition limits the animals left to die to the five חטאות. So everything else is clearly offered, and the suggestion seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Maybe they die, but only in the בית הבחירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought these animals die too, but specifically in the בית הבחירה. So the פסוק teaches that they are offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the five חטאות die anywhere, but these die in the בית הבחירה. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains the mistaken idea that the פסוק needed to rule out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תשא ובאת' could have suggested a new kind of dying: the five חטאות may die anywhere, but these animals would have to die inside the בית המקדש. The next words, 'ועשית עולותיך', rule this out and teach that they are offered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said': it brings in a mistaken idea the source comes to rule out
'In any place'
'It teaches us': the source is needed to correct that mistake

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the five sin offerings die in any location,
but these must die in the Temple
— so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mistaken idea (מהו דתימא) that the פסוק comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These animals die too, but only inside the בית הבחירה, unlike the five חטאות that die anywhere
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the offspring and תמורה of these קרבנות are offered on the מזבח
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'one might think' was not a silly idea. 'תשא ובאת' could have pointed to a special death inside the בית המקדש, and 'ועשית עולותיך' teaches that they are offered instead.

steps.title: Quoting the line: Are all sacred animals the same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that 'רק' teaches that not all קדשים follow this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: One might think all sacred animals are like this. So the פסוק says 'רק קדשיך', 'Only your holy things'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting another line from the ברייתא. This sets up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught that offspring and replacement animals of קדשים are brought and offered. Then it said the word 'רק' limits this, so it does not apply to every kind of קרבן. The גמרא now wants to look closely at this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred animals set aside as קרבנות
The פסוק teaches (literally: 'learning to say')
'Only': a word that limits or excludes something

phrases.english: The master said:
One might think that all sacred animals are the same?
The verse teaches: 'Only your holy things.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל אַף כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with the line about bringing the animals to the בית הבחירה, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא says the word 'רק' excludes some קדשים from the rule that their offspring are offered.

steps.title: Whose offspring could be excluded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offspring 'רק' could exclude. An עולה cannot give birth, and a חטאת's offspring is already known to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of which קרבן? If of an עולה, it is a male and cannot give birth! And if of a חטאת, we have a tradition that its offspring is left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It cannot find any offspring that the word 'רק' would need to exclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be a male animal, so it can never have offspring. The offspring of a חטאת is one of the five חטאות that are left to die, and that is already known from a tradition. So the word 'רק' seems to have nothing left to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of an animal
A burnt offering, which must be a male animal
A sin offering
We have a tradition (passed down, not learned from a פסוק)
They are left to die

phrases.english: The offspring of which offering?
If of a burnt offering, it is a male,
and it is not able to give birth!
And if of a sin offering,
we have a tradition that they are left to die!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the ברייתא quoted in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'רק' excludes the offspring of some קדשים from being offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Look at every possible case: an עולה has no offspring, and a חטאת's offspring is already known to die. So 'רק' has nothing to exclude.
